cases.explain: "Гул" is the subject of the intransitive verb "стихает" (is dying down), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: До продажи вишневого ___ мы все волновались, страдали.
cases.translation: Before the sale of the cherry orchard we were all anxious, we suffered.
cases.explain: The noun names what was sold, and "продажа" (sale) takes a genitive object, giving "сада."

cases.sentence: Отчего же письмо не взяли к ___?
cases.translation: Then why wasn't the letter taken to the doctor?
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (to/toward) always governs the dative case, giving "доктору."
"Целовать" (to kiss) is a transitive verb whose direct object takes the accusative case: "руку."

cases.sentence: Слышно, как вдали стучат ___ по дереву.
cases.translation: You can hear them striking the tree with an axe far away.
cases.explain: "Стучать" (to strike/knock) names the instrument used without a preposition, so it takes the instrumental case: "топором."

cases.translation: Yes, life in this house is over.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" (in) marking a stationary location takes the prepositional case: "доме."

cases.sentence: Не могу без ___, не знаю, что вот делать с руками.
cases.translation: I can't live without work, I don't know what to do with my hands.
cases.explain: The preposition "без" (without) always governs the genitive case: "работы."

cases.sentence: А я в Харьков уезжаю сейчас. Вот с этим ___.
cases.translation: And I'm leaving for Kharkov right now. On this very train.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with/on) here governs the instrumental case: "поездом."

cases.sentence: И только слышно, как далеко в саду топором стучат по ___.
cases.translation: And all you can hear is them striking the tree with an axe far away in the orchard.
cases.explain: The preposition "по" (against/along) with "дерево" here governs the dative case: "дереву."

reading.ru: Действие четвертое.
reading.question: What does this stage direction mark at the start of the passage?
options: A scene change within Act Two
reading.correct: The beginning of Act Four
reading.explain: The text opens with the heading 'Act Four,' signaling the final act of the play.

reading.ru: Нет ни занавесей на окнах, ни картин.
reading.question: What do the stage directions say about the room's windows and walls at the start of Act Four?
options: They are freshly decorated for a party
There are no curtains on the windows and no pictures
The pictures have been replaced with new ones
reading.correct: There are no curtains on the windows and no pictures
reading.explain: The opening stage direction states there are no curtains on the windows and no pictures, showing the house has been stripped bare.

reading.ru: Это пришли прощаться мужики.
reading.question: Why is there a noise (гул) heard offstage early in the act?
options: The peasants have come to say goodbye
reading.correct: The peasants have come to say goodbye
reading.explain: The text explains the offstage noise as the peasants who have come to say farewell.

reading.ru: Спасибо, братцы, спасибо вам.
reading.question: What does Gaev's voice say to the peasants offstage?
options: He scolds them for being late
He thanks them, addressing them as 'brothers'
He asks them to leave immediately
reading.correct: He thanks them, addressing them as 'brothers'
reading.explain: Gaev's offstage voice says 'Thank you, brothers, thank you,' expressing gratitude to the peasants.

reading.ru: Народ добрый, но мало понимает.
reading.question: According to Yasha, what is his opinion of the common people (простой народ)?
options: They are kind but understand little
reading.correct: They are kind but understand little
reading.explain: Yasha remarks that the common people are kind ('добрый') but understand little ('мало понимает').

reading.ru: Она не плачет, но бледна.
reading.question: How does Lyubov Andreevna appear when she enters with Gaev after saying goodbye to the peasants?
options: She is not crying, but she is pale
reading.correct: She is not crying, but she is pale
reading.explain: The stage direction says she is not crying but is pale, and her face trembles because she cannot speak.

reading.ru: Ты отдала им свой кошелек, Люба.
reading.question: What does Gaev reproach Lyubov Andreevna for doing?
options: Selling the house without telling him
Giving her purse away to the peasants
Inviting too many guests to the farewell
reading.correct: Giving her purse away to the peasants
reading.explain: Gaev tells her, 'You gave them your purse, Lyuba. That's not right,' scolding her generosity.

reading.ru: Из города не догадался привезть, а на станции нашел только одну бутылку.
reading.question: Why does Lopakhin only have one bottle of champagne for the farewell toast?
options: He forgot to buy champagne in town and found only one bottle at the station
The shop in town was closed for a holiday
He decided to save money and buy only one bottle
reading.correct: He forgot to buy champagne in town and found only one bottle at the station
reading.explain: Lopakhin explains he didn't think to bring champagne from town, and at the station he found only one bottle.

reading.ru: Это шампанское ненастоящее, могу вас уверить.
reading.question: What does Yasha say about the quality of the champagne after drinking it?
options: It is the finest champagne he has ever tasted
It is too sweet for his taste
reading.correct: It is not real/genuine champagne
reading.explain: Yasha assures the others that the champagne is not genuine ('ненастоящее').

reading.ru: Господа, имейте в виду, до поезда осталось всего сорок шесть минут.
reading.question: What time-related warning does Lopakhin give after checking the clock?
options: Only forty-six minutes remain before the train
There is no train until tomorrow
They have all day to pack
reading.correct: Only forty-six minutes remain before the train
reading.explain: Lopakhin looks at the clock and warns that only forty-six minutes remain before the train departs.

reading.ru: Я все болтался с вами, замучился без дела.
reading.question: Why does Lopakhin say he wants to go to Kharkov and work again?
options: He is bored of idleness and worn out from having no work
He wants to escape Trofimov's criticism
He has run out of money
reading.correct: He is bored of idleness and worn out from having no work
reading.explain: Lopakhin says he has been loafing about with everyone and is worn out from having nothing to do.

reading.ru: Не размахивай руками.
reading.question: What piece of advice does Trofimov give Lopakhin as a parting word?
options: Stop waving his arms around (a habit)
reading.correct: Stop waving his arms around (a habit)
reading.explain: Trofimov advises Lopakhin, 'Don't wave your arms,' urging him to break the habit.

reading.ru: Возьмите вашу гадость.
reading.question: What does Varya do with Trofimov's galoshes?
options: She polishes them and returns them politely
She throws them onto the stage, calling them 'nastiness'
She hides them so he cannot leave
reading.correct: She throws them onto the stage, calling them 'nastiness'
reading.explain: Varya, from another room, shouts 'Take your nastiness' and throws the galoshes onto the stage.

reading.ru: Я весной посеял маку тысячу десятин и теперь заработал сорок тысяч чистого.
reading.question: What business success does Lopakhin boast about to Trofimov?
options: He sold the cherry orchard for a huge profit
He sowed a thousand acres of poppies and made forty thousand rubles profit
He opened a bank in Kharkov
reading.correct: He sowed a thousand acres of poppies and made forty thousand rubles profit
reading.explain: Lopakhin boasts he sowed a thousand desyatinas of poppies in spring and cleared forty thousand rubles.

reading.ru: Человечество идет к высшей правде, к высшему счастью, какое только возможно на земле.
reading.question: What idealistic claim does Trofimov make about humanity's direction?
options: Humanity is moving toward higher truth and the highest happiness possible on earth
Humanity is doomed to repeat its mistakes
Humanity will always be ruled by the wealthy
reading.correct: Humanity is moving toward higher truth and the highest happiness possible on earth
reading.explain: Trofimov declares that humanity is advancing toward higher truth and the greatest happiness possible on earth, placing himself in the front ranks.

reading.ru: Мама вас просит, пока она не уехала, чтобы не рубили сада.
reading.question: What request does Anya relay to Lopakhin and Trofimov before her mother leaves?
options: That they hurry to the station immediately
That the orchard not be cut down while her mother is still there
That they say goodbye to Firs personally
reading.correct: That the orchard not be cut down while her mother is still there
reading.explain: Anya says her mother asks that the orchard not be cut down while she is still present.

reading.ru: Долголетний Фирс, по моему окончательному мнению, в починку не годится, его надо к праотцам.
reading.question: What does Yepikhodov say about old Firs?
options: Firs should be promoted to head servant
Firs is beyond repair and, in his opinion, should join his ancestors (i.e., is near death)
Firs should go to Paris with Yasha
Firs has already left for the hospital
reading.correct: Firs is beyond repair and, in his opinion, should join his ancestors (i.e., is near death)
reading.explain: Yepikhodov remarks that the aged Firs is 'not fit for repair' and, in his final opinion, should join his ancestors.

reading.ru: Через шесть дней я опять в Париже.
reading.question: What does Yasha say he will be doing in six days?
options: Visiting his mother in the countryside
reading.correct: Back in Paris again
reading.explain: Yasha says that in six days he will be back in Paris, showing his eagerness to leave Russia.

reading.ru: До продажи вишневого сада мы все волновались, страдали.
reading.question: According to Gaev, how did the family feel before the sale of the cherry orchard was finalized?
options: They were indifferent to the outcome
They were arguing constantly over money
reading.correct: They were anxious and suffering
reading.explain: Gaev says that before the sale of the cherry orchard they were all anxious and suffered, but calmed down once it was decided.

reading.ru: Я подготовлюсь, выдержу экзамен в гимназии и потом буду работать, тебе помогать.
reading.question: What does Anya promise to do to help her mother in the future?
options: Study, pass her school exam, and then work to help her mother
Take over management of the orchard
reading.correct: Study, pass her school exam, and then work to help her mother
reading.explain: Anya tells her mother she will prepare, pass her exam at the gymnasium, and then work to help her.

reading.ru: Приехали ко мне англичане.
reading.question: What surprising business news does Pishchik share?
options: Englishmen came to him and found white clay on his land
He has decided to become a farmer himself
reading.correct: Englishmen came to him and found white clay on his land
reading.explain: Pishchik excitedly explains that Englishmen came to his estate and found a deposit of white clay in the ground.

reading.ru: Она привыкла рано вставать и работать, и теперь без труда она как рыба без воды.
reading.question: How does Lyubov Andreevna describe Varya's second worry — Varya's situation without her usual work?
options: Varya is delighted to finally rest
Varya is used to rising early and working, and without work now she is like a fish out of water
Varya has found a new job she loves
Varya no longer wants to live at the estate
reading.correct: Varya is used to rising early and working, and without work now she is like a fish out of water
reading.explain: Lyubov Andreevna says Varya is used to early rising and hard work, and without it now she is like a fish out of water, having grown thin and pale.

reading.ru: Вот и кончилась жизнь в этом доме.
reading.question: What does Varya say as she looks over the emptied house one last time?
options: Life in this house has come to an end
The house will soon be rebuilt
She wants to buy the house herself
The house was always empty like this
reading.correct: Life in this house has come to an end
reading.explain: Varya remarks that life in this house has now ended and will not return.

reading.ru: Помню, когда мне было шесть лет, в троицин день, я сидел на этом окне и смотрел, как мой отец шел в церковь.
reading.question: What childhood memory does Gaev recall while looking at the window one last time?
options: Sitting at that window at age six on Trinity Sunday, watching his father walk to church
Learning to read at that window with his mother
Watching the cherry trees bloom for the first time
Playing billiards with his father as a child
reading.correct: Sitting at that window at age six on Trinity Sunday, watching his father walk to church
reading.explain: Gaev remembers that at six years old, on Trinity Sunday, he sat at that window watching his father walk to church.

reading.ru: О мой милый, мой нежный, прекрасный сад!
reading.question: How does Lyubov Andreevna address the cherry orchard in her final farewell?
options: As a burden she is relieved to leave behind
As her dear, tender, beautiful garden/life/youth/happiness
As a place she never truly loved
As property she regrets not selling sooner
reading.correct: As her dear, tender, beautiful garden/life/youth/happiness
reading.explain: In her farewell, Lyubov Andreevna calls the orchard 'my dear, my tender, beautiful garden,' equating it with her life, youth, and happiness.

reading.ru: Слышится отдаленный звук, точно с неба звук лопнувшей струны печальной.
reading.question: What mysterious sound is described near the very end of the play, as Firs lies alone?
options: A distant sound like a snapped string, sad and fading, coming as if from the sky
Church bells ringing in the distance
The sound of a train whistle
reading.correct: A distant sound like a snapped string, sad and fading, coming as if from the sky
reading.explain: The stage direction describes a distant sound resembling a snapped string, mournful and seeming to come from the sky, just before Firs is left in silence.
